THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_SESSION: P084 was UNGATEABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and last night's one-root-cause diagnosis was incomplete. Cause 1, correctly diagnosed last night: the validation scripts' own interpreter wrote 11 .pyc files into the tree and validate_cli.py then found them. Cause 2, found tonight and NOT previously recorded: release-gate check 2 runs ruff with its working directory set to the product root, which writes .ruff_cache into the tree, and check 6 then re-executes validate_cli.py, which asserted that NO cache directory existed. The gate created the condition it then failed, one check earlier, every single run. Measured by running check 2 and check 6 in the gate's own order on a clean tree. Had only cause 1 been fixed, tonight would have produced a second BLOCKED verdict on the same product and the night would have looked like last night.
WHY_THAT_MATTERS_BEYOND_P084: A fix verified against a diagnosis is only as good as the diagnosis. Cause 1 was reproducible standalone, which is exactly why cause 2 stayed hidden: running the script by hand from a clean tree never shows what the harness leaves behind. The general rule is now in PRODUCT_BUILD_GUIDE.md: a check whose own execution, or whose harness's execution, can create the condition it tests is not a check. Run every scanner twice from a clean tree, and once after the harness that will invoke it has done its own work.
WHAT_WAS_NOT_DONE: The release gate was NOT edited. Its ruff step wants the treatment its pytest step already has (-p no:cacheprovider, or RUFF_CACHE_DIR outside the tree). That one-line change belongs to the owner, not to an unattended session that would be editing the instrument that judges its own output. The product-side scanner was narrowed instead, to the two claims the product owns.
